clusters.state_of_play: The Ebola outbreak in DR Congo, the deadliest in its history and driven by the rare Bundibugyo species, has surpassed 5,021 cases and 2,500 deaths, spreading 18 times faster than the deadliest outbreak on record with roughly one death every 30 minutes. A UN official warns it is growing exponentially across an area bigger than France, and funding for the response is set to run out within weeks. Health workers face attacks, unpaid labor, and fear amid weak infrastructure, community resistance, instability, and mobile populations like gold miners. The US has warned of a long road ahead, and the WHO has begun delivering 70,000 doses of the Ervebo vaccine to Congo, of which 16,000-plus have arrived; the vaccine is most effective against the Zaire strain but may offer partial protection against Bundibugyo.
